aarti.pad1: I bow to the Lord of the Raghus, the treasury of compassion, through whom the worldly knowledge that sees difference falls away. ॥1॥
aarti.pad2: He is the moon that gladdens the night-lilies of Raghu's line; Brahmā and Śiva serve his lotus feet. ॥2॥
aarti.pad3: He is the bee in the lotus of his own devotees' hearts; his lovely form is like countless gods of love. ॥3॥
aarti.pad4: He is the sun to the overpowering darkness of delusion, and a fierce fire to the dense forest of ignorance. ॥4॥
aarti.pad5: He is the pot-born Agastya to the ocean of pride, and generous; he delights the gods and breaks the burden of the earth. ॥5॥
aarti.pad6: He is Garuḍa to the swarms of serpents that are attachment and the rest, a lion to the elephant of Kāma, and Murāri, the foe of Mura. ॥6॥
aarti.pad7: His lotus feet are the ship across the ocean of worldly existence; he is Jānakī's beloved, the root of bliss. ॥7॥
aarti.pad8: He is the swan in the pool of Hanumān's love, the wish-granting cow to those who are free of desire, and compassionate. ॥8॥
aarti.pad9: Rāma, the ornament of the three worlds and fathomless in virtue, is the abode of rest, says Tulasīdāsa. ॥9॥
